field.label: Classify connections
field.help: Name each connection's application with nDPI and keep the servers it names in pf tables, aliases in Firewall: Aliases. It reads a copy of what the firewall sees and changes no traffic. Off, the classifier stops and its aliases leave Firewall: Aliases - switched off instead where a rule or a setting still names one.

field.label: Interfaces
field.help: Where connections are read. None chosen: every internal interface - one with an address of its own and no gateway. No port is made promiscuous.

field.label: Application tables
field.help: A table of its own for each application chosen, appcontrol_ and its name, holding servers it was seen with. Every nDPI category has a table without being chosen: appcontrol_cat_ and its name. The list is the installed nDPI's.

field.label: Blocked applications
field.help: Each application chosen is blocked: a table of its own, as in Application tables, and a block rule of this plugin's on it, ahead of the rules of Firewall: Rules, so a new connection from any interface to a server in the table is dropped - on every port, so another service on the same address is blocked as well. A connection nDPI names as it from its packets is cut once its window is judged, some 10 to 70 seconds after it began: its pf states killed by its two ends and, with Cut in hardware on in os-xgs-npu's XGS: Settings, dropped on the coprocessor first. Its server goes into the table only when the firewall's own resolver gives that address for the name the connection carried, since a device can write any name to any address, and only when nothing named that address, within the address expiry, as an application not blocked; else that connection alone is cut. Those it named earlier and still remembers are cut at Apply. A guess, a connection whose beginning was not seen, and one to the firewall, a host of its internal networks or an address not on the internet - private, shared or unique-local - are never cut. Choosing a protocol that carries others - TLS, QUIC, HTTP, DNS - blocks every application it carries. None chosen, or classifying off: nothing is blocked.

field.label: Log what is blocked
field.help: Log each packet the block rules drop, in Firewall: Log Files: Live View, under the rule's description: Application Control: block and the application's name. Off, they are counted on the Applications tab, not logged.

field.label: Address expiry (seconds)
field.help: How long an address stays in a table once unseen: the Expire of the tables' aliases, carried out by OPNsense's own cron. Seen again, its time starts again.
